body:
Strongly +1 for this idea. I ended up here to create a similar issue.

---

We are wasting too much time on terminal for waiting executions:

```
rust        -  215ms  -   "via 🦀 v1.61.0 "
```

Before we _run_ the following above command, we can firstly look up the `~/.cache/starship/binary-cache.toml` file to check if binary's digest exist. If so, we can get the version there. 

I'm not sure if we have to call, for example, `shasum /usr/local/bin/python3` each time to get _current_ digest of binary.

@matchai Why did you stop working on that PoC? Got stuck on somewhere?

It would be great to prioritize this issue.

> I'm not sure if we have to call, for example, `shasum /usr/local/bin/python3` each time to get current digest of binary.

The [solution in the POC](https://github.com/starship/starship/commit/8bb76e08eeacdbeb7b51a2aee1c7cc9dbfba2b81#diff-99de0e02e304ce79cd846826f01d33518e77b58028402717877fd91eadd3a081R171-R179) is to produce a hash out of the binary size, ctime, mtime, and permissions to avoid having to shasum the whole binary, which would be much much faster.
The reason to do so would be to support version managers like nvm, brew, and asdf, which may update the binary in-place.

> Why did you stop working on that PoC? Got stuck on somewhere?

The solution was working pretty well, but it was clear that the codebase would require some refactoring to best implement the solution.
Specifically, the binary cache should be integrated into [`exec_cmd`](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/master/src/context.rs#L310) in a way that allows us to selectively retrieve from the cache when appropriate (e.g. ignoring `git` commands) while remaining compatible with our [`cmd_mock`](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/master/src/utils.rs#L126) implementation in testing.

I simply haven't had a whole lot of time to dedicate to this recently. Hopefully, someone can pick up the remaining integration work to get this out the door 😄
